proposed_rating.why: 3 high and 1 medium findings; U1 blocks reliance on the results

checks.title: Model profile, intended use and risk tier
checks.finding: Central-bank tone classifier (LLM): label each sentence of FOMC statements, minutes, speeches and press conferences as hawkish, dovish or neutral, and aggregate the labels into a policy-tone index. The tone index is a monthly input to rate-path views and scenario narratives. Risk tier Medium. The validation tests the model against that use.

metrics.name: Central-bank tone classifier (LLM)
metrics.purpose: Label each sentence of FOMC statements, minutes, speeches and press conferences as hawkish, dovish or neutral, and aggregate the labels into a policy-tone index
metrics.use: The tone index is a monthly input to rate-path views and scenario narratives
metrics.vendor: Third-party LLM via API (version not pinned in the source)

checks.title: Every answer can be turned into a label
checks.finding: 100.0% of 1428 answers contain a label word; 0 do not.

checks.title: Answers follow the instruction (one word)
checks.finding: The prompt asked for one word. 100.0% of answers start with a label, but the median answer is 37 words long (an unrequested explanation); 5.0% name more than one label and 3.6% contain a negated label ('not hawkish'). Because the label always comes first, the usual 'first label word' parser and a strict 'first word' parser agree here, but a lenient parser would misread answers if the model ever put the explanation first. The extra text also multiplies cost and latency.
checks.recommendation: Constrain the output (one token, a fixed label set or structured output) and log raw answers.

The sentence provides a factual update on the current state of the labor market without indicating a clear bias towards tightening or easing of monetary policy. The mention of a faster pace of payroll employment expansion and a decline in the unemployment rate could be seen as positive indicators, but the qualification that the unemployment rate remains elevated suggests a cautious tone. checks.title: Accuracy against simple benchmarks (macro-F1, 3 test splits)
checks.finding: Mean macro-F1 is 0.552 for the model against 0.570 for a TF-IDF logistic regression trained in seconds on the same training data, 0.440 for a keyword lexicon and 0.217 for always answering the majority class. The model is significantly better than TF-IDF on 0 of 3 splits and significantly worse on 0 (paired bootstrap, 95%). The added cost, opacity and vendor dependence of the LLM buy no accuracy.
checks.threshold: significantly better than TF-IDF on every split
checks.recommendation: Do not adopt the zero-shot LLM over the benchmark; fine-tune (or use a fine-tuned encoder) and re-assess against the same benchmarks.

checks.title: Stability of accuracy across test splits
checks.finding: Macro-F1 ranges from 0.532 to 0.580 across the three splits.

checks.title: Repeatability: the same sentence asked in separate calls
checks.finding: 257 sentences appear in more than one test split and were classified in separate calls; the model gave the same label every time for 99.2% of them.

checks.title: No systematic bias toward one class
checks.finding: The model answers 'neutral' for 70% of sentences, against a true share of 48%. It finds only 28% of hawkish sentences (recall), against 48% of dovish ones. Errors are not random: they lean one way, so they will not average out in an index.
checks.recommendation: Recalibrate (class thresholds on label probabilities) or fine-tune; monitor the predicted class mix in production.

checks.title: Wrong-direction errors (hawkish read as dovish, or the reverse)
checks.finding: 7.7% of hawkish or dovish sentences are given the opposite stance (TF-IDF: 16.8%). Most errors are therefore misses (a stance read as neutral) rather than reversals.

checks.title: Errors by document type, period, sentence structure and length
checks.finding: Overall macro-F1 is 0.552. No segment with 50 or more sentences is more than 0.10 below it.

checks.title: The tone index built from the model tracks the true index
checks.finding: Across 27 years with at least 10 labelled sentences, the model's yearly index correlates -0.10 with the index from the true labels (TF-IDF: 0.50). The slope of model on truth is -0.07, the average offset is -0.158 (negative = too dovish) and the sign is wrong in 14 years. The model's index carries little of the true year-to-year variation. With 10-85 sentences per year the true index is itself noisy, but the benchmark tracks it far better.
checks.recommendation: Do not feed the index into decisions without rescaling; validate rescaling out of sample, or replace the classifier.

checks.title: Minimum functionality: unambiguous sentences
checks.finding: [Live model: TF-IDF + logistic regression (benchmark); not the model under review, shown for information.] 69% of 52 unambiguous template sentences are labelled correctly (hawkish 65%, dovish 55%, neutral 100%).
